{"findings": [{"file": "src/completion_queue.zig", "line": 320, "severity": "major", "category": "correctness", "title": "getResult returns error.Closed on an open, non-drained queue, which no caller can tell from a real drain", "body": "The change deletes the `drained` computation (`node == null and self.closed and self.pending.isEmpty()`) and returns `error.Closed` unconditionally when `completed` is empty. The two states it now merges are genuinely different: 'closed and fully drained' (terminal) and 'open with operations in flight' (a stale wake). The function still holds the mutex at the point where it could distinguish them, so the information is available and is thrown away.

The comment tells the caller to 'treat it as spurious and re-poll' when it 'knows it never closed the queue'. That condition is not generally satisfiable: `close` is documented as thread-safe (line 151) and the module header (lines 38-49) describes exactly the shape where another task closes a queue the driver is waiting on. A driver selecting over such a queue cannot know whether the `error.Closed` it just got is the real drain or a stale wake.

Consequence: a correct driver following the documented contract breaks out of its loop on a spurious `error.Closed` while operations are still in flight. Per the module header (lines 14-20) those operations are heap-backed and owned by the driver, so the queue is torn down with the only pointers to them still inside it — leaked memory and dropped results. The previous `std.debug.assert(drained)` was loud; the replacement is silent and points the failure at data loss instead of a crash. It also removes the only detector of the upstream protocol bug, and adds no replacement instrument (no counter, no log), so that bug is now invisible in every build mode.

Note `wait` and `timedWait` are immune to the same stale wake because they re-loop; only `getResult` cannot. A local fix that keeps the loudness: return `error.Closed` only when `drained` is true, and for the not-drained case either keep the assert or widen `Result` with a distinct error the select caller can re-poll on deliberately."}, {"file": "src/completion_queue.zig", "line": 84, "severity": "major", "category": "docs", "title": "The public docs still state the strict wake contract that getResult no longer honors", "body": "Three public doc sites keep the old contract and now contradict the code:

- Line 86, the `signal` field: 'The future protocol depends on the strict reading of a wake: a completion is takeable, or the queue is drained.'
- Lines 280-283, the future-protocol block: 'The registered wait completes when a completion is ready to be taken or the queue is drained; `getResult` then pops one like `next`, or reports `error.Closed`.'
- Lines 52-57, the module header: the select result is 'what `wait` would have returned'. `wait` returns `error.Closed` only when closed and fully drained, so this is now false.

The new caveat lives only inside the body of `getResult`, where a caller of `select(.{ .io = &cq, ... })` never reads it. A caller reading the header treats `error.Closed` as terminal, which is precisely the behavior that leaks in-flight operations. Documentation that contradicts behavior is worse than either alone here, because the wrong reading is the destructive one."}, {"file": "src/group.zig", "line": 252, "severity": "major", "category": "correctness", "title": "Group.getResult has the same stale-wake exposure and reports success silently", "body": "The change states the stale wake as a property of this waiter shape: a signal dispatched for a registration a concurrent winner canceled can outlive the select's signal accounting and land on a re-used waiter slot. `Group`'s future protocol (lines 240-313) is the same shape, byte for byte in `asyncWait`/`asyncCancelWait`/`WaitContext`, and parks on the same kind of futex word.

`Group.getResult` returns `void`, so a stale win reports 'the group drained to zero pending tasks' with tasks still running. There is no error the contract can express and no assert to catch it, so the caller proceeds past its select and typically releases the group frame and the task contexts that the still-running tasks are using. That is a use-after-free rather than the leak the CompletionQueue site produces, and it is silent in every build mode.

If the upstream protocol bug is real enough to change `CompletionQueue`, this site needs at least a detector (re-read the counter in `getResult` and fail loudly when it is non-zero) in the same change; otherwise the fix hardens one of two identical sites and leaves the more dangerous one unmarked."}]}
